named_confounds: origin composition shift (unknown-origin share rises from 40% to 70% after 1876)
rationale: Estimand: for each genre, mean DISTANCE_TRAVEL passage rate in late works (year>=1876) minus early works, each work weighted equally; then averaged with equal weight across the 8 genres. Every work has exactly one passage, so work rates are 0 or 1. Overall effect is +0.0021 with a 95% bootstrap CI (resampling within genre x period cells) of [-0.023, 0.025]. Robustness checks: restricting to high-date-confidence works gives +0.0027 [-0.039, 0.036]. An OLS on late, adjusted for genre, origin, date_confidence, log editions and log author productivity, with SEs clustered by author, gives -0.012 [-0.035, 0.012]. Stratifying by origin gives inconsistent signs (UK -0.017, US -0.024, unknown +0.026). Year is associated with origin: unknown-origin works go from 40% to 70%. Year is only weakly related to date_confidence, n_editions and productivity. Decade means show no monotonic trend (about 0.08-0.15, plus noisy early decades with few works). Coverage: 6766 works, but only 752 are pre-1876, which makes early estimates imprecise. The cited passage IDs are DISTANCE_TRAVEL-tagged passages from well-dated early and late works; they show that the construct occurs in both periods and say nothing about a trend. Conclusion: there is no robust historical shift. The estimate is near zero, the CI includes zero, and the sign flips under adjustment and stratification.
